sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Slemuin is a being of the Otherworld in the Irish tale of Odras. He is the smooth bull of the spirit world. The death-queen Mórrígan took a cow from Odras so the cow could stand with the royal bull of the other world. Bold Odras set out to win the cow back. She went down toward the great caves of the Otherworld that open near the old royal seat of Cruachan. There a sleep of wonder came over her. She fell asleep beneath a great oak and never woke, for Mórrígan turned her into the small lake that takes her name. The bull Slemuin remains beside the queen of the spirits. The girl who came seeking her cow became water. The bull and the lake hold the two halves of the old tale of the cow that was taken away.
